February 14, 1938. Afternoon Translation.

Sin Shun Pao (a Japanese owned paper in Chinese language):

DISSOLUTION OF PING TSE ZOEN CLUB

The Ping Tse Zoen Club (丙子社) is a political body. It was established in spring 1936 after the election of new members to the Chinese Ratepayers' Association having been approved by the local Tangpu and was supported by Messrs Tu Yaeh-sung (杜月生) and Wong Shiao-lai (王曉籟). Its members were officials of the Tangpu and the Citizens' Federation. It received a monthly subsidy of $1,000.

There is another body called the Shan Zoen Club (商社) which is directed by Mr. Wong Yien-soong (王延松). Members of the Shan Zoen Club were all prominent merchants. When it was dissolved after the departure of Mr. Wong from Shanghai, the monthly subsidy of $1,000 of the Shan Zoen Club was transferred by the anti-Wong elements to the Ping Tse Zoen Club.

Ostensibly, the Ping Tse Zoen Club is directed by Mr. Tsu Yang-wu (朱養和), a follower of Mr. Wang Mei-yuin (汪曼云) of the local Tangpu, who was an associate of Mr. Wu Kai-sien (吳開先), Executive Committeeman of the Tangpu and was supported by him. Tsu was responsible for the finances of the Club.

As the $1,000 subsidy was more than enough for the Club's expenses, it was suggested that the Club should provide members with cigarettes etc. Negotiations were opened with Tsu over these matters and disputes arose among the members of the Ping Tse Zoen Club over the question of money.

Following the change in the general situation, the subsidy to the Club ceased and important figures of the Club left Shanghai with the result that the Club was dissolved.

At one time, the Ping Tse Zoen Club established a Ping Tse News Agency (丙子通信社) which sometimes supplied news items to newspapers, mainly of a nature to extort money.

Sin Shun Pao of Feb.12:

INEFFICIENT POLICE WATCH GIVES RISE TO TERRORIST ACTIVITIES IN FOREIGN SETTLEMENTS

During the past few days, cases of assassination wherein the victims have been decapitated have been discovered daily, causing great anxiety to the residents of the International Settlement and the French Concession. The fact that terrorist gangs are so active and that anti-Japanese elements and murderers are able to act so freely is mainly due to the inefficient watch maintained by the authorities of the Foreign Settlements. In contrast to the Foreign Settlements, the Japanese Army protected district of Hongkew presents an extremely calm appearance. For this reason, a large number of intelligent persons are applying for permission to remove into Hongkew.

1938年2月14日。下午译文。

《新顺报》（一家中文日报，属日本人所有）：

丙子社解散

丙子社是一个政治团体。它成立于1936年春，在当地党部批准中国纳税人协会新成员当选后成立，并得到杜月生先生和王曉籟先生的支持。其成员为党部和市民联合会的官员。该社每月获得1,000元的津贴。

另有名为商社的团体，由王延松先生领导。商社的成员均为知名商人。在王先生离开上海后该社解散时，反王派系将商社每月1,000元的津贴转给了丙子社。

表面上，丙子社由朱養和先生领导，他是当地党部汪曼云先生的追随者，也是党部执行委员吳開先先生的 associate（关联人士/同僚），并得到吴的支持。朱负责该社的财务。

由于1,000元的津贴足以支付该社开支，有人建议该社应向成员提供香烟等物品。就此事项与朱进行谈判，导致丙子社成员之间因金钱问题发生争执。

随着总体局势的变化，对该社的津贴停止，社内重要人物离开上海，结果该社解散。

丙子社曾设立丙子通信社，有时向报纸提供新闻稿件，主要性质为敲诈勒索。

2月12日《新顺报》：

租界警方监视不力导致恐怖活动滋生

过去几天，每天都能发现受害者被斩首的暗杀案件，引起国际租界和法租界居民的极大焦虑。恐怖帮派如此活跃，抗日分子和凶手能够如此自由行动，主要是由于外国租界当局维持的监视效率低下。与外国租界相比，日军保护的虹口地区呈现出极其平静的景象。因此，大量有识之士正在申请许可搬入虹口。

Subject (in full) Particulars regarding the membership of the "Ping Ts Club."
Made by D.S. Pnaruzyn Forwarded by ____

Further to the attached file and remarks of D.C. (Crime
and Special Branches) thereon, C.D.C. 230 again called at the
"Ping Ts Club" on 21-9-37 and found that both the club and the
Ping Ts News Agency have temporarily ceased functioning,
probably due to the charge framed by the Police against Chaung
Yau (张 友 ) and Woo Pen-eu (吴 平 欧 ), two employees of the
aforesaid Agency, for extortion.
For this reason no information can for the present be
secured relative to the membership of the Club.
The premises are at present sheltering a number of
refugees.

D. S.

D. C. (Crime and Special Branches).

Extortion by Member of News Distributing
Organisation.
------------------------------

At 10.50 p.m. 10/9/37 C.D.C. 213 brought to the
station from the Merryland Cabaret 377 Yu Ya Ching Road
a male Chinese one Chaung Yau ( 莊 岳 ) 24, Chengchow,
newsreporter, Sz Soo Li, 3, Yunnan Road whom he had
arrested on a charge of extortion at the instigation
of the manager of the cabaret one George Monzon Philli-
pino, residing on the premises.

C.D.C. 213 and the undersigned enquired and
ascertained that at about 9.45 p.m. even date a cigarette
tin, containing a quantity of ammonia, had been thrown
through one of the windows of the cabaret. A short
time after, the complainant stated he received a tele-
phone call from an anonymous source saying that if he
did not close his cabaret a bomb would be thrown into
it on the next day. Later at about 10.15 p.m. the
accused came to the cabaret and communicated with the
complainant that he was a newsreporter and that he had
come to investigate the throwing of the ammonia. The
complainant stated that he told the accused that no
such incident had occurred, whereupon the accused said
that he knew that it had occurred and that he would
report it in the usual way and that it would appear in

新闻分发组织成员实施敲诈勒索。
---

1937年9月10日晚上10点50分，C.D.C. 213从余姚路377号的美乐舞厅将一名中国男子莊岳（24岁，郑州人，记者，住云南路慈淑里3号）带至警局，此人因涉嫌在舞厅经理、居住于该处的菲律宾人George Monzon的唆使下实施敲诈勒索而被捕。

C.D.C. 213和本人进行了讯问并查明，当晚约9点45分，一个装有大量氨水的香烟盒被扔进舞厅的一扇窗户。不久后，投诉人称接到一个匿名电话，称如果他不关闭舞厅，第二天就会有人向舞厅投掷炸弹。随后在约晚上10点15分，被告来到舞厅并与投诉人联系，声称自己是记者，前来调查投掷氨水事件。投诉人称他告诉被告并未发生此类事件，但被告说他知道此事已经发生，并将按常规方式进行报道，该报道将刊登在

to-morrow's editions of the Chinese newspapers. He,
however, went further, and said that for the sum of
$30.00 he would suppress the item of news. This the
complainant agreed to and paid over the sum in question,
this transaction was witnessed by one Sung Keh Zung
(孫克仁) 23, Ningpo, residing on the cabaret premises,
on the completion of the business, the complainant
immediately called C.D.C. 213 who was on duty inside
the Cabaret, explained the circumstances of the case
and requested the apprehension of the accused for
extortion.

Interrogated at the station the accused admitted
the offence. Questioned regarding how he came to know
of the incident at the cabaret he said that he had
been told to go and investigate by the manager of the
|| Le Nyi News Distributing (麗尼通訊社) Agency, 4a-
gs Soo Li, 3 Yunnan Road, and he further stated that
the manager, one Woo Peh Bu (吳半厂) 35, Shanghai,
above address, had instructed him that should he be
able to obtain money for the promise of suppressing
the news he should accept same.

Detectives visited the offices of the News Distri-
buting Agency at Yunnan Road, and brought the manager
Woo to the station for interrogation. He stated that

次日出版的中文报纸上。然而，他进一步表示，只要支付30.00元，他就会压下这条新闻。投诉人同意了这一点并支付了这笔款项，此交易由居住在舞厅内的孫克仁（23岁，宁波人）见证。交易完成后，投诉人立即呼叫了在舞厅内执勤的C.D.C. 213，解释了案情，并请求以敲诈勒索罪逮捕被告。

在警局受审时，被告承认了罪行。当被问及如何得知舞厅发生的事件时，他说他是受云南路慈淑里3号麗尼通訊社经理的指派前去调查的，他还进一步陈述说，经理吳半厂（35岁，上海人，住址同上）指示他，如果他能以承诺压制新闻为条件获得钱财，他就应该接受。

侦探前往云南路的新闻分发社办事处，并将经理吴带至警局进行讯问。他陈述说

he received the information of the throwing of the ammo-
nia from an unknown source. He denied having instructed
the accused to try to obtain money for the suppressing
of the news. However, when confronted with the manager
the accused re-affirmed his statement regarding this.
In view of the foregoing Supt. Mason D.D.O. "A"
was informed and on his instructions the accused Chaung
and the manager Woo are being detained at this station
pending further instructions as to the disposal of this
case.
With regard to the throwing of ammonia into the
dance hall, it was thrown through one of the windows
facing Yu Ya Ching Road, without causing any damage.
C.D.C. 213 made enquiries at the time but was unable
to obtain any information as to the thrower, owing to
the fact that there were very few people in the neigh-
bourhood.

that at 3.00 a.m. even date he received through the
post, a letter containing a threat to bomb the
Merryland Cabaret located at 377 Yu Yn Ching Road,
of which he is manager, should he fail to suspend
business within the next two days.

On the 17/9, the undersigned enquired and
ascertained that the letter contained the threat
was typewritten by an educated person
as the handwriting is very well formed and the
composition of the letter as a whole is well conceiv-
ed and carried out. (Translation of letter appended
herewith). The letter was apparently posted from the
16th District Post Office Rue de Consulat.

It was elicited that the complainant, when
opening the cabaret had had some trouble with the
management of the New World Hotel with regard to the
water supply which is controlled from the New World
Hotel. This disagreement however, was amicably
settled and as far as the complainant is concerned
no importance is attached to the possibility of the
above mentioned people having any connection with
the threat as contained in the letter, nor could any
information be obtained which might lead the detec-
tives to believe that the management of the New World
Hotel were using this method as a reprisal owing to
the former dispute.

On 13/9/37 the complaint in this case was also
the complainant in a case of Extortion (F.I.R. 703/37)
against two male Chinese, named Cheung Yau (張有 )
and Yee Fan Au (葉凡奧 ). newsreporter and manager,

1937年9月14日下午4时30分，报案人报告称，同日凌晨3时，他通过邮政收到一封信，信中威胁称，如果他在接下来两天内不停止营业，将炸毁位于虞洽卿路377号的“百乐门舞厅”（Merryland Cabaret），他是该舞厅的经理。

9月17日，具名者经查询查明，这封包含威胁内容的信是由一名受过教育的人用打字机打出的，因为字迹非常工整，且整封信的构思和执行都很完善。（信的译文附后）。该信显然是从领事馆路（Rue de Consulat）第16区邮局寄出的。

经查明，报案人在开设舞厅时，曾因供水问题与新世界酒店（New World Hotel）的管理层发生过一些纠纷，该供水由新世界酒店控制。然而，这一分歧已友好解决，就报案人而言，他不认为上述人员可能与信中所含威胁有任何关联，也未获得任何可能使侦探相信新世界酒店管理层因先前纠纷而采取此种报复手段的信息。

page_data.en:
Translation

To the employees of the Merryland Cabaret.

The enemy's guns have been fired from North China to
Shanghai. For the purpose of saving our nation and seeking
existence, we are obliged to offer resistance. The hostilities
in Shanghai have been taking place for four weeks and our loyal
and brave soldiers have been continuously sacrificing their lives
in the serious fights to defend our land. As we are the people
of China, we should subscribe our valuables that we have, to our
Government, but during such tense situation, you dare actually
open your cabaret for business, and the charming dancing girls
lure the youths to diminish their ambitions. We want to ask
you that were China extinct, how would you to use your large
amount of money? You should know that all the bank notes will
become waste paper, should China become extinct. Now we give
you a time limit of two days within which, you have to suspend
your business, failing to comply with this, we will immediately
bomb your cabaret, making it become a piece of burned land, and
by so doing we will not mind our sacrifice, as we have decided
to reach our object. Should a first bomb fail to take effect,
there will be 2nd and 3rd ones. Hoping you will awake immediately.

Bomb National Salvation Association.
12/4/37.

译文

致百乐门舞厅全体员工。

敌人的炮火已从华北射向上海。为了拯救我们的国家并寻求生存，我们不得不进行抵抗。上海战事已持续四周，我们忠诚勇敢的士兵在保卫国土的激烈战斗中不断牺牲生命。作为中国人民，我们应该将我们的贵重物品捐献给政府，但在如此紧张的局势下，你们竟敢开设舞厅营业，且迷人的舞女引诱青年消磨意志。我们要问你们，如果中国灭亡了，你们如何使用大量的金钱？你们应该知道，如果中国灭亡，所有钞票都将变成废纸。现给予你们两天期限，在此期限内，你们必须停止营业，若不遵从，我们将立即炸毁你们的舞厅，使其成为一片焦土，为此我们不惜牺牲，因为我们已决心达到目的。如果第一枚炸弹未生效，将有第二枚和第三枚。希望你们立即醒悟。

炸弹救国会。
1937年4月12日。
